intervention_or_comparison: unpassivated control, compound 1, and compound 2-treated perovskite films
kpfm_observable_and_direct_result:
KPFM-derived surface work function
4.77 eV (control); negligible change with compound 1; 4.68 eV with compound 2.
pl_family_observable_and_direct_result:
steady-state PL intensity
Increased for compounds 1 and 2 relative to the control.
Steady-state PL intensity is directly relevant to the present optical comparison.
evidence_grounded_claim: Both Fc compounds increased steady-state PL intensity, whereas a substantial KPFM-derived work-function decrease occurred only with compound 2.
complementary_interpretation: PL distinguishes the passivation-related emissive response from KPFM-derived work-function tuning across the same treatment series.
interpretation_limit: KPFM and luminescence measurements used corresponding treatment groups but separate specimens/geometries. Co-trending does not establish that the work-function change caused the luminescence response.

pl_family_observable_and_direct_result:
PL-mapping intensity and spatial distribution
Compound 2 showed a substantial mean decrease and much-improved homogeneity relative to the control in C60-contacted stacks.
evidence_grounded_claim: The strongest narrowing of the CPD distribution (compound 2) accompanied the strongest and most spatially uniform PL quenching at the perovskite/C60 interface.
complementary_interpretation: KPFM maps energetic uniformity, while PL mapping reports the spatial uniformity of charge extraction for the same interlayer series.
interpretation_limit: The maps were not spatially registered. In the C60-contacted PL stack, lower PL was interpreted as stronger extraction rather than as poorer emissive quality; the association is noncausal.
